correctness.rationale: The exact reduction of the source's Eqs. (1)–(3) gives the invariant physical simplex and an initially positive infected fraction. The ratio \(r=s/i\) has derivative \(\dot r=\gamma-\eta r-\eta i r(r+1)\); its threshold \(r=\gamma/\eta\) is crossed strictly downward, establishing the complete peak dichotomy. Scalar comparison proves \(i\to0\), stable forcing gives \(r\to\gamma/\eta\), and stable-filter bounds justify \(w=-pi+p(2R+1)i^2+O(i^3)\). Thus \(\dot i=-Ki^3+Li^4+O(i^5)\). Inverting \(\frac{d}{dt}(i^{-2})=2K-2Li+O(i^2)\) yields the exact universal coefficients and the \(O(t^{-3/2}\log t)\) remainder. The bundled standalone verifier checks symbolic identities and finite numerical diagnostics. It is not evidence for the infinite-time quantifiers by itself, and no independent audit is asserted.

value.rationale: The initiating article identifies tricritical parameters and numerically estimates an exponent but leaves transient trajectory shape and correction coefficients unquantified. The positive initial-condition-independent \(t^{-1}\) term measures slow susceptible-ratio adjustment that the scalar cubic normal form omits. The exact initial infected/susceptible ratio cutoff separates transient outbreak growth from monotone decline for every admissible initially infected state. This answers two natural finite-time questions in the source model without claiming the already established exponent or a result for stochastic or spatial populations.
